subject: Re: Pricing Annex — micro-banding language & soft-cap exemption
message_1_headers:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing Annex — micro-banding language & soft-cap exemption
message_1_body:
Jordan —

Thanks for the call this morning. As promised, attaching our proposed edits to the Order Schedule and Pricing Annex to clarify the micro-banding trigger and the proposed limited soft-cap exemption. High-level summary of the changes we made: 

- Micro-banding: added an explicit threshold definition (billing window = calendar month, metric = consumed inference tokens) and a three-step taper for band transitions (immediate, 30-day smoothing, 90-day stabilization).
- Soft-cap exemption: added a customer-initiated exemption clause for force majeure-style capacity events with a 60-day mutual review window and a one-time 30% temporary uplift allowance.
- Clean-up: clarified measurement granularity and removed ambiguous "business-need" language that could be interpreted broadly.

We believe these edits preserve the economic protections Acme asked for while giving your team a clear path to short-term capacity exceptions during onboarding surges. 

Please find the redline attached (Acme_OrderSchedule_redline_v3.docx) and the microband matrix (pricing-exhibit_microband-matrix.xlsx). If you want, Laura can walk your procurement/legal team through the smoothing math tomorrow.

Next steps: please confirm if the 60-day review window is acceptable and flag any specific language you'd like us to reword.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Acme_OrderSchedule_redline_v3.docx (docx)
Attachment: pricing-exhibit_microband-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

message_2_body:
Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the doc. A couple quick clarifying asks from procurement/legal so we can take to our CFO: 

1) On the "three-step taper" — can you add a small worked example for a 3-month ramp so we can see the effective per-token rate over each month? Your matrix is helpful but the legal team wants a simple illustrative table embedded in the exhibit.

2) The proposed 30% temporary uplift: is that on top of the committed rate or a capped effective discount reduction? In other words, will Acme be charged the committed rate + uplift, or will the uplift reduce the discount floor? We need the math spelled out.

3) The 60-day mutual review — can you confirm who signs the review off (procurement lead + Redwood regional rep), and whether either side can request an interim billing true-up if the exemption period extends beyond 60 days?

Sara (cc) will lead the legal redline; I expect their markup within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Jordan
Senior Procurement Manager
AcmeCloud

message_3_headers:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecloud.com>, Sara Patel <s.patel@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing Annex — micro-banding language & soft-cap exemption
message_3_body:
Hi Jordan / Sara —

Thanks — happy to make those clarifications. Short answers first, then an inline excerpt we'll add to the exhibit: 

1) Worked example: we'll insert a three-line table showing a 3-month onboarding with usage 100% -> 220% -> 130% of committed baseline. The effective per-token rates will show the taper effect and the temporary uplift arithmetic.

2) 30% uplift semantics: the uplift is an additive surcharge on top of the commercial rate for the exemption period (i.e., committed rate * (1 + uplift %)). It is NOT a reduction of the discount floor. We will add explicit formulae and a numeric example.

3) Sign-off and true-up: proposed sign-off parties are Acme Procurement Lead + Redwood Regional Sales Director (we provide name and contact in the exhibit). Either party can request an interim billing true-up if the exemption runs past 60 days; the true-up will be capped to corrections for measurement errors and egregious overconsumption during the exemption. The idea is to avoid surprise retroactive reconciliations while enabling both sides to correct for sustained anomalies.

Inline excerpt we'll insert in the Pricing Annex (summary):
"Micro-banding example and soft-cap exception mechanics: For clarity, during a declared exemption period the effective monthly invoice will equal the committed monthly fee multiplied by (1 + uplift %). If usage during the exemption exceeds 150% of committed baseline for more than 30 consecutive days, the parties will initiate a mutual review; if the exemption extends beyond 60 days the parties may agree to a pro-rata true-up limited to measurement errors or documented excess consumption attributable to the exemption event."

Laura will attach a marked PDF with the table and the exact formulae later today. Irene from Legal is cc'd for any final contract language validation.

Best —
Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

message_4_body:
Laura / Karthik —

Thanks for the clarifications; Acme legal's quick read is generally OK with the approach. Two final edits we propose (attached as a PDF with tracked changes):

1) Narrow the definition of "exemption event" to explicitly include data center outage, provider-wide capacity failure, or cloud provider region degradation. Remove generic "onboarding surge" language — procurement will approve onboarding exceptions on a case-by-case basis but wants them documented as business-initiated exceptions rather than automatic.

2) For transparency, require Redwood to provide token-level export of peak windows during the exemption period (CSV export) to support any interim true-up. This is a limited data deliverable for billing reconciliation only.

If you can accept those two edits, Acme will sign the amended Order Schedule and route to our CFO for final signature next week. For the record, Jordan — please confirm the procurement lead's contact details for the approval flow.

Sara Patel
Senior Counsel, AcmeCloud
